An opera house in Cairo, opened on 1 November 1869 and the first in Africa and the Middle East. It burned down on 28 October 1971.

The khedive Ismail, Egypt's ruler, had it built of wood in about six months for the celebrations of the opening of the Suez Canal. Ismail wanted Cairo to look like a European capital, and he laid out a new quarter in the style of Haussmann's Paris around it. The first show was Verdi's Rigoletto.

Ismail asked Giuseppe Verdi for a new opera on an Egyptian theme. The result, Aida, had its premiere at the Cairo house in December 1871, and has been tied to Egypt ever since.

The spending on such projects helped push Egypt into debt and then into British control. The opera house stayed at the centre of Cairo's cultural life for a century. After the fire a new Cairo Opera House, a gift from Japan, opened in 1988 in another part of the city.
sum: An opera house in Cairo, opened on 1 November 1869 and the first in Africa and the Middle East. It burned down on 28 October 1971.
